description: Abandoned But Not Forgotten — an interactive scrollytelling tribute to NASA's discarded hardware on the Moon and Mars. Three.js starfields, interactive hotspots, a lunar lander mini-game, WebAudio transmissions, and a memorial wall for lost missions.
summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten: NASA's Off-World Heritage (https://nasa-website-one.vercel.app/) is an interactive educational web application that transforms the history of discarded space hardware into an immersive, story-driven experience.

What We Developed:
We built a responsive, single-page digital archive cataloging 24 iconic rovers, landers, and probes across the Moon, Mars, Venus, and deep space. Key interactive features include first-person audio voice logs, a clickable planetary surface radar map, a 1959–present exploration timeline, a "Probe Builder" physics simulator, and a gamified Explorer Passport with printable certificates.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
Technical space history is often presented through dense, passive text that struggles to engage students. Our platform replaces static reading with hands-on exploration—letting users hear first-person stories from dormant explorers like Opportunity and Ingenuity, test engineering designs against harsh extraterrestrial environments, and earn badges through interactive trivia.

Why It Is Important:
Beyond celebrating human ingenuity, these silent machines are priceless archaeological and material-science artifacts. Preserving their stories inspires the next generation of STEM innovators while raising awareness around space heritage and planetary protection as humanity prepares to return to the Moon and beyond.
details:
Project Overview

  • Project Title: Abandoned but not Forgotten: NASA's Off-World Heritage
  • Live Web Application:https://nasa-website-one.vercel.app/
  • Target Audience: School-age space enthusiasts, students, and casual learners.
  • Core Mission: Transform dense technical history into an engaging, story-driven digital experience that highlights NASA's robotic explorers, landers, descent stages, and scientific instruments left behind across the solar system.

Key Interactive Features

  1. Comprehensive Relics Archive (24 Artifacts):
    • Covers hardware across The Moon (e.g., Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 17 Lunar Rover, ALSEP instruments), Mars (e.g., Sojourner, Opportunity, Spirit, Ingenuity Helicopter, InSight), Venus (Venera 13, Pioneer Venus), and Deep Space / Asteroids (Voyager 1 & 2, Pioneer 10, Cassini, New Horizons, Philae).
    • Features detailed engineering specs, mission histories, and breakthrough scientific discoveries.
    • Built-in text-to-speech voice logs that allow users to listen to immersive, first-person stories told from the perspective of each dormant explorer.
    • An interactive HTML5 Canvas radar map that lets users scan planetary surfaces and click on target landing markers to inspect historical sites on the Moon, Mars, and Venus.
    • An interactive timeline tracing humanity’s robotic footprints across space exploration history from 1959 to the present.
    • An interactive engineering challenge where students customize probe components (chassis materials, power sources like solar vs. RTGs, and scientific payloads) and test their probe’s survival against harsh planetary environments (extreme vacuum, Venusian heat, Martian dust storms).
    • Tracks inspected relics and passed trivia challenges to rank users up to Interplanetary Archivist, offering a gamified badge collection and an official printable certificate.

Scientific & Educational Impact

  • Planetary Heritage: Teaches students about planetary protection, future space archeology, and how historical hardware serves as priceless test subjects for material science.
  • Active Engagement: Moves away from passive reading by combining quizzes, simulation mini-games, and audio logs to boost retention and spark curiosity for STEM fields.
